title: Hydroxyethyl Cellulose/Polyethylene Glycol Cryogel Containing Strontium Species Derived From Strontium Oxide Precursor for Antibacterial Activity and Domestic Wastewater Disinfection
content:
By rupturing bacterial cell membranes and encouraging intracellular protein leakage, Sr-incorporated HEC/PEG cryogels demonstrate potent broad-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacy. The cryogels' potential as reusable antimicrobial biomaterials is highlighted by their maintained antibacterial efficacy during repeated use.


ABSTRACT

It is important for developing safe and effective materials for wastewater disinfection to reduce the hazard posed by waterborne pathogens. Thus, hydroxyethyl cellulose/polyethylene glycol (HEC/PEG) loaded with SrO-derived strontium-containing cryogel (Sr-HEC/PEG) was synthesized via freeze-drying. The antibacterial activity of HEC/PEG and Sr-HEC/PEG cryogel materials against representative waterborne bacteria was assessed. The results showed that Sr-HEC/PEG cryogel at 40 mg/L exhibited significant antibacterial activity up to log 6.2 CFU/mL. Gram-negative bacteria were killed within 15 to 30 min in time-kill studies, whereas Gram-positive bacteria needed longer time. Similarly, results exhibited good antibiofilm properties due to its potential in inhibiting bacterial adhesion. The Microtox assay showed low bioluminescence inhibition toward Aliivibrio fischeri under the tested acute exposure conditions. In domestic wastewater, the cryogel demonstrated further practical applicability by achieving viable bacterial counts below the plate-count detection limit after 40–90 min of contact time and by demonstrating reusability over five successive cycles. Based on these aforementioned data, Sr-HEC/PEG cryogel with effective antibacterial activity shows no potential toxicity and demonstrates good operational stability, making it a promising sustainable disinfectant material for practical water/wastewater disinfection technologies.
